newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank sets repo at unchanged 4.10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank sets repo at unchanged 4.10 pct.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Tuesday left its key interest rate, the repo rate, unchanged at 4.10 percent at its weekly tender.
The operation will run from February 26 to March 5.
The Riksbank said bids had to be made by 0900 GMT on February 25.
Yesterday, a Reuters poll of 12 economists had found that seven did not expect the bank to make any change to the repo rate due mainly to the current weakness in the crown.

Some had expected the Riksbank to wait to see the results of an inflation forecast survey due out on Wednesday while others said the bank would not move until its next inflation report was released on March 20.
Three of the economists had said the chances of a cut were 50/50 while two had expected the rate to be lowered.
Expectations of a cut were fuelled last week when the Consumer Price Index for January showed a monthly rise of just 0.1 percent for a year-on-year fall of 0.1 percent.
This was the fourth consecutive month that Sweden has shown a negative annualised inflation rate and it came as a surprise to the market.
The repo rate, which is the Riksbank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity, was last lowered on December 17 at the same time as the central bank's last quarterly inflation report.
Last year the repo rate was cut 25 times, taking it down to its current level of 4.10 percent fom 8.91 percent.
